issues.message: No source for this 2014 VF-3 itself was found: the travels, table, rapids, spindle and sizes are today's VF-3's (the product page, saved 2026-11-10; the layout drawing of 2/23/2023). The travels (40 x 20 x 25 in) agree with dealers' listings, among them a 2013 unit (docs/research/2026-11-06-lab-machines.md); the enclosure's sheet metal is assumed unchanged since 2014 [INFERENCE].
The sources disagree on the spindle nose to table by 0.1 in: 4.1 to 29.1 in on the layout drawing (p. 4), 4.2 to 29.2 in on the product page. The drawing is used: it is the more detailed of the two.

The trunnion's model is not confirmed: its plate is not readable in the photos (the visit list, item 10). It is a Haas TR (two supports, one platter; the 2026 guide, p. 8), and the TR160 by elimination: the TR210 is 49.6 in long, more than the 48 in table it stands on, and the TR310 needs a VF-6 [INFERENCE]. The TR160's platter, speeds and sizes are used as labelled stand-ins; the A and B ranges are the same for every TR.

Which way +A and +B turn this trunnion is not confirmed: the 2011 rotary manual gives the right hand rule for the tool's motion, but notes that table movements depend on 'the equipment, parameter settings, or five-axis programming software' (p. 35). Where A and B home is not cited either.

The 2012 manual disagrees with itself on a rotary feed: 'G01 A90. F50. will rotate the A-Axis 90 degrees at 50 degrees per second' (p. 173), against Setting 34: the feed is in inches per minute and the control computes the angular feed from the part's diameter (p. 271). It also says 'Rapid moves are not allowed' in its five-axis notes (p. 173), while G00 takes an A address (p. 181). Decision 0036 chooses.

Haas's sources disagree on the TR160's swing: 'Max swing at 90°: 14.4” (366mm)' in the 2004 TRT manual (p. 7), 'Part Swing Max 17.5 in' on today's TR160 page. Neither is used for the twin's geometry, which is sized from the photos; the 2004 note's 3.1 mm from the platter to the A axis is a stand-in [INFERENCE].

Today's TR160 page asks for 'NGC software version 100.21.000.1130 or later'; dealers' listings of the TRT160 and TRT210 ask for 'software version 18.00 or later' (docs/research/2026-11-06-lab-machines.md; a Classic control's numbering [INFERENCE]), so the trunnion does not tell which control this unit runs.
Which control this unit runs (Classic or Next Generation) is not confirmed (the visit list, item 11); the 2012 Classic manual is the nearest edition to its 12/2014 date.
The tool changer does not show in the photos: it is left out of the twin (Daniel's rule, 2026-10-24), and a program's tool change is logged, not simulated (plan, Phase 6).
